title: Detectives
summary: This is a collection of Sherlock Holmes stories by Arthur Conan Doyle, gathering the detective's cases from the Strand Magazine period into one volume. The contents list includes well-known tales such as "A Scandal in Bohemia," "The Red-headed League," "The Speckled Band," "The Blue Carbuncle," "Silver Blaze," and "The Dancing Men," along with several others from the later casebook and the empty-house return. The excerpts shown include "The Five Orange Pips," in which the young John Openshaw brings Holmes a sinister series of letters marked K.K.K. that have haunted his family across generations, and the closing pages of a tale about a hydraulic engineer, a fire at a lonely house, and a severed thumb. The sampled middle passage is not Holmes fiction at all but a literary essay by Doyle on Walter Scott's novels and the qualities of soldiers in fiction. The collection mixes mystery, deduction, and a few digressive non-fiction pieces, with the Holmes stories as its core.
